frame.objective: Determine if Cotral Lab should expand its sales from employers to consumers, and if so, which consumer segments and value proposition to target.
constraints: Cotral Lab has not publicly disclosed its plans to sell directly to consumers.
The company’s current sales are primarily to employers, with no indication of a shift to consumer markets.
Financial data is not publicly available, so economic assumptions are speculative.
alternatives: Do not enter the consumer market at all, focusing on employer sales.
Target a niche consumer segment (e.g., audiophiles, fitness enthusiasts) with a premium value proposition.
Expand to a broader consumer market (e.g., all workers) with a mass-market value proposition.
Focus on B2B2C (Business-to-Business-to-Consumer) models, such as partnerships with employers for employee wellness programs.
Investigate the feasibility of a subscription model for hearing protection among consumers.

searches: why people do not wear earplugs at music events
trial of earplugs at music events
Hearing protection adoption among young adults, barriers to use, and consumer behavior in music events.

T1.claim: Gen Z’s hearing damage at music events stems from a combination of social stigma, lack of awareness, and inadequate hearing protection options, driving demand for discreet, user-friendly solutions.
T1.who_benefits: Cotral Lab, hearing protection manufacturers, and employers seeking employee wellness programs.
T1.why_behaviour_changes: Gen Z avoids wearing earplugs due to embarrassment, lack of awareness, and perceived discomfort, prompting a shift toward discreet, user-friendly solutions.
T1.how_value_is_captured: Premium pricing for discreet, high-quality hearing protection, partnerships with employers for employee wellness programs, and subscription-based models.
assumptions: Gen Z prioritizes social acceptance and discretion when choosing hearing protection.
employers are willing to invest in hearing protection programs for employee wellness.
Discreet, high-quality hearing protection is a viable alternative to traditional earplugs.
predictions: Gen Z will increasingly adopt discreet hearing protection solutions if they are perceived as socially acceptable and user-friendly.
Employers will prioritize hearing protection programs for employee wellness, driving demand for employer partnerships.
